children: Forget about an official Red Ryder Carbine-Action 200-shot range model air rifle—the toys kids are waiting to unwrap this holiday season are squishy, loud, and, as always, pricey.
Compiling a list of the most popular toys depends on who you ask. Amazon
and Target
are probably the most popular destinations for kids under 10, while kids 10 and up would most likely prefer their parents shop at Best Buy
for game consoles, laptops, earbuds, and, of course, the digital download code for Grand Theft Auto VI
Doubling as both collectibles and a calming sensory tool, squishies—including dumpling squishies—are still at the top spot at both Amazon
and Target

. The tactile toys are made from slow-rising polyurethane foam that gives a satisfying squeeze and are available in almost unlimited shapes and sizes—from raindrop-shaped squishies to animal-shaped squishies to squishies shaped like a stick of butter.

For creative types, Stickerbox lets kids (and some adults) make their own stickers using AI to generate designs and is equipped with thermal printing that avoids costly ink refills. The $130 Stickerbox is designed to block inappropriate prompts to make sure each sticker is kid-friendly.

Expanding on its "dinosaur hatching" phenomenon from last year, Primal Hatch now allows kids to hatch their own megalodon. Put the egg in the tank, add water, and watch while a shark is “born.” Best part? The color-changing, explosive hatching action can be repeated over and over. Primal Hatch is available at Amazon
, Walmart
, and Target
with Amazon
offering the best price of $35.
Got a young recycler at home? The Crunchinator and ChompSaw let kids crush empty soda cans and cut up cardboard boxes instead of tossing them.
Designed by a NASA engineer, the $35 Crunchinator enables kids to crush and smash objects in what the company calls “the most satisfyingly destructive ways possible.”

To make use of all those empty Amazon boxes, the $130 Chompshop Chompsaw cuts old cardboard boxes into any shape and any creation to make dioramas, classroom projects, costumes, and whatever else kids can dream up.

For more mindless entertainment, there’s the flying orb ball toy, a “hand-controlled mini drone flight spinner” that can fly, hover, and even respond like a boomerang, all with RGB lighting that creates a mesmerizing light display.
Mattel
is continuing to cash in on the KPop juggernaut with a new line of KPop Demon Hunters toys, while Disney
is leaning on a holiday evergreen—a Toy Story figurine line featuring Woody, Jessie, Buzz, Slinky, Rex, and Forky in movie-inspired scale.

Electronics are still a favorite among teens, tweens, and adults with the Consumer Technology Association finding that at least 87% of adults plan to buy tech gifts this holiday season. The most popular for 2026 includes Apple
AirPods 5, Sony
cameras, and Ray-Ban Meta
smart glasses, showing that the most-wanted gifts still come with a charging cable.
Target
, Amazon
, and Best Buy
all have the Nintendo

Switch 2 Console as one of its bestselling items this holiday season. The next generation of the Nintendo Switch comes with a $500 price tag but gives gamers three play modes: TV, tabletop, and handheld. While the console is compatible with all Nintendo Switch games, it still can’t get you to Vice City.
The toys might change every year—still squishy, still loud, and still pricey—but the mission never does: find the right one before someone else does.

title: From squishies to can crushers: The toys on the top of Santa's list
